exposure: Hirayama disease diagnosis (based on clinical criteria: insidious onset nonprogressive chronic upper limb weakness and atrophy in teens or early twenties without sensory deficits and coarse tremors)
outcome: loss of attachment of posterior dura and subjacent lamina
crescent-shaped epidural intense enhancement (thickness and vertebral level extension)
cohort: The study included eighteen patients assessed for clinical and radiological Hirayama disease.
finding: The study found a high prevalence of specific MRI abnormalities in patients with Hirayama disease, including cord flattening (100%), loss of posterior dural attachment and anterior displacement (100%), and crescent-shaped epidural enhancement (100%), often extending to the dorsal cord.
cross-section timing: Patients were assessed at a single point in time, with a mean age of 20.33 years, for existing chronic upper limb weakness and atrophy.
